title: Microsoft–AFL-CIO: labor-tech partnership and neutrality framework

observations.claim: Microsoft and the AFL-CIO announced an AI partnership on 11 December 2023.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The stated goals are worker and labor-leader education, incorporation of worker expertise into technology development, and public-policy collaboration.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The announcement also describes a neutrality framework for future organizing by AFL-CIO affiliates.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: The public record frames the mechanism as open dialogue and partnership rather than a deployment-specific collective-bargaining agreement.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: No named employer use case, data source, model, threshold, adverse decision or worker remedy is disclosed.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

observations.claim: No public source in this lane gives the AFL-CIO authority to pause, override or reverse a Microsoft customer or internal employment system.
limits: Bounded to the cited public record and instrument posture.

findings.claim: Education and design input can improve worker capacity to participate, but participation without decision power is not sufficient counterpower under Wave 04.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: The neutrality framework may expand the future ability to bargain, but it is analytically distinct from a binding AI clause.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: The partnership should not be promoted to proof that workers control a named deployment or receive an appeal and remedy.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.

findings.claim: Deployment effects, worker-selected representatives at a specific worksite, enforceable information rights and system revision remain open.
limits: No unpublished term, universal prevalence, named-company intent, or complete worker outcome is inferred.
